title: Disk full on inventory-service host

symptoms.message: The inventory-service host reported no space left on device, causing all write operations to fail. Log rotation had stopped and temporary files had consumed the remaining 4 GB. Reads were still succeeding but any attempt to persist state returned ENOSPC.

error_signature: 2026-03-05T02:28:41Z ERROR inventory-service [storage] write failed: no space left on device (errno=ENOSPC path=/var/data/inventory)
root_cause: Disk exhaustion caused by unrotated log files and accumulated temporary export files

fix_steps.step: Identify and delete stale temporary export files under /var/data/inventory/tmp
fix_steps.note: Freed 3.2 GB immediately

fix_steps.step: Force log rotation on the inventory-service nodes
fix_steps.note: Freed additional 800 MB and restored write capacity

resolution: Deleted temporary export files and forced log rotation, restoring disk space and write operations within 28 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify largest temporary and log files, delete or rotate them, verify free space above 20%, and add disk-usage alerting at 80%.
impact: 22% of users could not complete inventory-dependent operations for 28 minutes.
lessons: Add disk-usage alert at 80% threshold
Schedule automated cleanup of temporary export files older than 24 hours

title: Memory leak in search-service causing OOM restarts

symptoms.message: The search-service pods were restarting every 30 to 40 minutes with OOMKilled status after RSS memory climbed from 512 MB to 1.8 GB over roughly 3 hours. Search latency spiked during the pre-restart ramp and users saw 503 errors immediately after each restart. Heap dumps showed large retained caches of parsed query ASTs that were never evicted.

error_signature: 2026-03-14T11:04:12Z FATAL search-service [runtime] OOMKilled: container exceeded memory limit 2Gi (rss=1847Mi); restarting pod search-service-7d9f8b-xk2pq
root_cause: Unbounded in-memory AST cache for parsed search queries introduced in release v3.1.0 caused memory to grow without bound

fix_steps.step: Restart the search-service pods to recover immediate availability
fix_steps.note: Restored service briefly but OOM restarts recurred within 35 minutes as the leak continued

fix_steps.step: Roll back to release v3.0.8 to remove the unbounded cache
fix_steps.note: Memory stabilised at 530 MB and OOM restarts stopped entirely

resolution: Rolled back to release v3.0.8 to remove the unbounded AST cache, stopping OOM restarts and stabilising memory usage.
runbook_summary: Restart pods for immediate relief, identify the leaking release via heap dump comparison, roll back to the last stable release, and add memory-usage alerting at 80% of limit.
impact: 30% of search users experienced intermittent 503 errors and elevated latency during the 55-minute incident window.
lessons: Require bounded cache sizes with eviction policies in all new code
Add heap-growth trending alert to catch leaks before OOM

title: TLS certificate expiry on auth-service

symptoms.message: Auth-service began rejecting all HTTPS connections at midnight when its TLS certificate expired. Clients received certificate-validation errors and could not authenticate. Internal services relying on mTLS also failed their handshakes.

error_signature: 2026-03-22T00:00:03Z ERROR auth-service [tls] certificate expired: CN=auth.internal notAfter=2026-03-21T23:59:59Z
root_cause: TLS certificate for auth-service expired because the 90-day renewal reminder was not actioned

fix_steps.step: Renew and deploy the TLS certificate for auth-service using the internal CA
fix_steps.note: Certificate renewed with a 1-year validity and hot-reloaded within 18 minutes

resolution: Renewed the expired TLS certificate and hot-reloaded it, restoring all auth connections within 18 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify expiring certificate, generate CSR, sign with internal CA, deploy to secret store, and trigger hot reload; add 30-day pre-expiry alert.
impact: 100% of users could not authenticate for 18 minutes.
lessons: Automate certificate renewal 30 days before expiry
Alert on certificates expiring within 14 days

title: Database connection pool exhaustion on checkout-api

symptoms.message: The checkout-api stopped processing orders when all 20 database connections in the pool were held by slow analytical queries that had leaked from a reporting job. New checkout requests queued until they timed out with a 503 response. Error logs showed repeated pool-exhausted warnings with a 30-second wait timeout.

error_signature: 2026-04-12T09:13:55Z ERROR checkout-api [db] connection pool exhausted: waited 30000ms for connection (pool_size=20 checked_out=20 overflow=0)
root_cause: Database connection pool size of 20 was too small when a runaway reporting job leaked connections and saturated the pool

fix_steps.step: Restart the application only without fixing the pool exhaustion
fix_steps.note: Checkout recovered briefly but the pool exhausted again within an hour as the leak continued

fix_steps.step: Increase the database connection pool size to 100
fix_steps.note: Pool headroom restored and checkout requests immediately began succeeding

fix_steps.step: Restart the checkout-api pods to clear leaked connections
fix_steps.note: Cleared all leaked connections and confirmed pool utilisation dropped to 8%

resolution: Increased the database connection pool size to 100 and restarted checkout-api pods to clear leaked connections, restoring checkout operations within 42 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify pool exhaustion via error logs, kill runaway connections, increase pool size, restart service, and add pool-utilisation alert at 80%.
impact: 40% of checkout users received 503 errors for 42 minutes during peak trading hours.
lessons: Separate reporting queries from the transactional connection pool
Set pool-utilisation alert at 80% to catch exhaustion early

title: Bad deployment broke payment-service

symptoms.message: Immediately after deploying release v4.2.0 of payment-service, the error rate climbed to 28% with NullPointerException traces in the logs. The new release had a missing null-guard on the card-type field that caused failures for 28% of payment requests where card type was omitted.

error_signature: 2026-04-18T14:31:02Z ERROR payment-service [processor] NullPointerException at PaymentProcessor.java:142 field=cardType value=null release=v4.2.0
root_cause: Release v4.2.0 introduced a null-pointer regression on the cardType field that was not caught in testing because the test suite did not cover null card types

fix_steps.step: Scale out the payment-service to absorb the elevated error load
fix_steps.note: Scaling out added more pods running the broken release and did not reduce the error rate

fix_steps.step: Roll back to release v4.1.9 to remove the regression
fix_steps.note: Error rate dropped to 0.1% within 5 minutes of rollback completing

resolution: Rolled back payment-service to release v4.1.9, eliminating the NullPointerException regression and restoring normal payment processing.
runbook_summary: Identify the breaking release from deployment history, roll back to the last known-good version, verify error rate drops, and add null-guard to the failing field before re-deploying.
impact: 28% of payment transactions failed for 35 minutes.
lessons: Add test cases for null card-type inputs before releasing payment changes
Never scale out a service that is failing due to a code bug

title: Upstream timeout cascade from notification-service

symptoms.message: The notification-service began timing out when calling the upstream email-relay provider, causing retries to pile up and exhaust the internal HTTP client thread pool. Downstream order-service calls to notification-service then started timing out at 10 seconds, causing order confirmations to be delayed. No emails were lost because messages queued in the outbox.

error_signature: 2026-04-25T15:59:44Z WARN notification-service [email-relay] upstream timeout after 5000ms (retries=3 provider=smtp-relay.internal host=relay01)
root_cause: The external email relay provider suffered a brief outage, causing timeout cascades into the notification-service retry loop

fix_steps.step: Reduce the upstream email-relay timeout to 2000ms and enable circuit breaker
fix_steps.note: Stopped thread-pool exhaustion and allowed the service to shed upstream load gracefully

fix_steps.step: Drain and reprocess the outbox queue once the relay recovered
fix_steps.note: All queued notifications delivered within 5 minutes of relay recovery

resolution: Reduced upstream timeout and enabled circuit breaker, preventing thread exhaustion; outbox messages delivered after relay recovery.
runbook_summary: Enable circuit breaker on the upstream dependency, reduce timeout to a safe value, check for queued messages, and reprocess once upstream recovers.
impact: 12% of users did not receive order-confirmation emails on time for 32 minutes.
lessons: All upstream HTTP clients must have a circuit breaker configured
Set timeout to 2 seconds for non-critical email relay calls

title: Cache stampede on inventory-service hot key

symptoms.message: A product-launch event caused the cache entry for SKU-99001 to expire under extremely high concurrent traffic. Thousands of simultaneous cache misses each triggered a full database read, spiking the database CPU to 95% and causing latency spikes across all inventory queries. The cache entry had a hard TTL of 60 seconds with no jitter.

error_signature: 2026-05-03T10:44:58Z WARN inventory-service [cache] stampede detected: key=sku:99001 concurrent_misses=3847 db_cpu_pct=95
root_cause: Cache stampede on a hot product key during a launch event caused by zero-jitter TTL and no request coalescing

fix_steps.step: Increase the cache TTL to reduce expiry frequency
fix_steps.note: A longer TTL did not help because the key had already expired and the flood was in progress; under burst traffic even a long TTL eventually expires

fix_steps.step: Enable request coalescing on the hot key to prevent parallel database reads
fix_steps.note: Collapsed thousands of concurrent misses into a single database read per key expiry

fix_steps.step: Warm the cache by pre-loading the top 100 product keys before the next launch
fix_steps.note: Prevented the first cache miss from being serviced at peak concurrency

resolution: Enabled request coalescing and pre-warmed the cache, eliminating the stampede and restoring normal inventory latency within 25 minutes.
runbook_summary: Enable single-flight request coalescing on hot keys, warm the cache with a pre-load job, add TTL jitter of ±10%, and monitor concurrent-miss rate.
impact: 20% of users experienced slow inventory responses and intermittent errors for 25 minutes during the launch event.
lessons: Always add TTL jitter to prevent synchronised expiry under high load
Pre-warm cache for known high-traffic events

title: Order queue backlog in order-service

symptoms.message: The order-service queue depth climbed from 0 to 180,000 messages in 20 minutes after a consumer crash left no active workers. Orders were accepted and enqueued but not processed, causing confirmation delays. The dead-letter queue began filling after message TTL expiry.

error_signature: 2026-05-11T08:19:33Z ERROR order-service [queue] no active consumers on queue orders.process depth=180432 dlq_depth=214
root_cause: All order consumer workers crashed due to an unhandled deserialization exception in a new message schema, leaving the queue unprocessed

fix_steps.step: Restart the order-service consumer workers with the previous message schema handler
fix_steps.note: Consumers restarted and began draining the backlog at 4,000 messages per minute

fix_steps.step: Move expired dead-letter messages to a replay queue for reprocessing
fix_steps.note: Recovered 214 orders from the dead-letter queue and confirmed delivery

resolution: Restarted consumer workers and replayed most dead-letter messages, draining the backlog within 48 minutes; a small number of messages with invalid schema were discarded.
runbook_summary: Identify consumer crash cause, restart consumers with safe schema handler, monitor drain rate, replay dead-letter messages, and add consumer liveness alerting.
impact: 18% of orders were delayed by up to 48 minutes; approximately 12 orders with corrupted schema could not be automatically recovered and required manual reprocessing.
lessons: Add consumer liveness alerts that fire within 2 minutes of all workers stopping
Schema changes must include a backwards-compatible deserialization fallback

title: Connection pool exhaustion on order-service database

symptoms.message: Order-service database connections were exhausted during a high-order-volume window when the pool hit its ceiling of 15 connections. Requests queued and timed out with database connection unavailable errors. The pattern closely matched INC-104 but on the order-service rather than checkout-api, with slightly different pool sizing.

error_signature: 2026-05-20T13:44:51Z ERROR order-service [db] connection pool exhausted: all 15 connections in use, timeout waiting for available slot (wait_ms=30000)
root_cause: Database connection pool size of 15 was insufficient for peak order volume, leading to pool exhaustion and request timeouts

fix_steps.step: Increase the database connection pool size to 80
fix_steps.note: Pool expanded and queued requests immediately began succeeding

fix_steps.step: Restart the order-service pods to clear stale held connections
fix_steps.note: Cleared 3 connections held by timed-out requests and confirmed pool utilisation at 12%

resolution: Increased the database connection pool size to 80 and restarted order-service pods to clear stale connections, restoring order processing within 38 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify pool exhaustion, expand pool size to appropriate capacity, restart service to clear stale connections, and monitor pool utilisation.
impact: 35% of order operations failed for 38 minutes.
lessons: Pool sizes should be set based on peak concurrency analysis, not defaults
Apply DB-POOL-RECOVERY runbook immediately when pool-exhausted errors appear

title: DNS resolution failure in payment-service

symptoms.message: The payment-service could not resolve the internal DNS name for the fraud-check API after a CoreDNS config change was pushed. All payment attempts that required fraud checking failed with a name resolution error, causing a 35% error rate for payment requests.

error_signature: 2026-06-02T19:09:44Z ERROR payment-service [dns] name resolution failed: fraud-check.internal: no such host (resolver=10.96.0.10:53)
root_cause: A CoreDNS configuration change removed the search domain entry for the internal services namespace, breaking DNS resolution for all internal service names

fix_steps.step: Revert the CoreDNS configuration change to restore the internal search domain
fix_steps.note: DNS resolution restored within 90 seconds of the CoreDNS config rollback

resolution: Reverted the CoreDNS configuration change, restoring internal DNS resolution and payment fraud-check calls within 22 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify failing DNS lookup, check recent CoreDNS config changes, revert the breaking change, verify resolution with nslookup, and add DNS health checks.
impact: 35% of payment requests failed for 22 minutes.
lessons: DNS configuration changes must be tested in staging with integration tests before production
Add CoreDNS health-check alerting

title: Recurring memory leak in search-service after feature flag enabled

symptoms.message: After enabling the real-time-suggestions feature flag in release v3.2.1, search-service memory climbed steadily from 600 MB to 1.9 GB over 4 hours before triggering OOMKilled restarts. The pattern was identical to INC-102: heap retained large unbounded in-memory caches with no eviction policy.

error_signature: 2026-06-14T09:29:01Z FATAL search-service [runtime] OOMKilled: container exceeded memory limit 2Gi (rss=1934Mi); restarting pod search-service-5c7b9d-mn4rw release=v3.2.1
root_cause: The real-time-suggestions feature in release v3.2.1 introduced another unbounded suggestion cache that grew without eviction, repeating the INC-102 pattern

fix_steps.step: Restart the search-service pods to recover immediate availability
fix_steps.note: Pods recovered but OOM restarts recurred within 40 minutes as the leak continued under the enabled feature flag

fix_steps.step: Roll back to release v3.2.0 to disable the leaking feature
fix_steps.note: Memory stabilised at 620 MB and OOM restarts stopped; confirmed identical pattern to INC-102

resolution: Rolled back to release v3.2.0 to remove the leaking suggestions cache, stopping OOM restarts and stabilising memory.
runbook_summary: Restart for immediate relief, identify leaking release via memory growth comparison with previous incidents, roll back, and enforce bounded cache policy before re-enabling feature.
impact: 33% of search users experienced intermittent 503 errors for 40 minutes.
lessons: Feature flags must be tested under sustained load before enabling in production
Any feature that introduces an in-memory cache must have a bounded size and eviction policy

title: CPU and thread saturation on notification-service

symptoms.message: The notification-service CPU reached 98% across all pods after a burst of 200,000 marketing emails was queued simultaneously. The thread pool saturated at 200 threads and new notifications were rejected with a thread-pool-full error. Async notification delivery fell behind by 15 minutes.

error_signature: 2026-06-22T15:00:11Z ERROR notification-service [thread-pool] pool saturated: 200/200 threads in use, rejecting task (queue_depth=48221 cpu_pct=98)
root_cause: Simultaneous bulk email campaign submission saturated the notification-service thread pool and CPU with no rate limiting on campaign ingestion

fix_steps.step: Throttle the campaign ingest rate to 5,000 messages per minute to shed load
fix_steps.note: CPU dropped to 62% and thread pool freed up within 3 minutes of throttling

fix_steps.step: Restart the notification-service pods to clear the thread-pool backpressure state
fix_steps.note: Clean restart confirmed thread pool at 12% utilisation with throttling active

resolution: Throttled campaign ingest rate and restarted notification-service pods, reducing CPU from 98% to 62% and clearing the thread-pool saturation.
runbook_summary: Identify the load source, throttle ingestion rate, restart pods to clear backpressure, and add per-campaign rate limiting to prevent recurrence.
impact: 14% of users experienced delayed notifications for up to 30 minutes.
lessons: Campaign ingestion must have rate limiting to prevent thread-pool saturation
Add CPU and thread-pool-saturation alerts at 80% threshold

title: Bad deployment on auth-service broke token validation

symptoms.message: Release v2.5.0 of auth-service introduced a breaking change to the token-signing key ID format. Tokens issued by new pods could not be validated by older pods and vice-versa, causing intermittent 401 errors as requests were load-balanced across mixed-version pods.

error_signature: 2026-07-05T11:15:33Z ERROR auth-service [jwt] token validation failed: unknown kid=v2.5-key-001 (known_kids=[v2.4-key-001]) release=v2.5.0
root_cause: Release v2.5.0 changed the JWT key ID format without backward compatibility, causing validation failures on mixed-version deployments during a rolling update

fix_steps.step: Roll back to release v2.4.3 to restore a single consistent key ID format
fix_steps.note: All pods converged to v2.4.3 within 4 minutes and 401 errors stopped immediately

resolution: Rolled back auth-service to release v2.4.3, restoring a consistent JWT key ID format across all pods and eliminating 401 errors.
runbook_summary: Identify the breaking release, roll back all pods to the last compatible version, verify error rate drops, and fix the breaking change before re-deploying.
impact: 45% of authenticated requests failed for 28 minutes during the rolling update window.
lessons: JWT key ID changes must be backward compatible across rolling update windows
Canary deployments must validate auth flows before full rollout

title: Bad config change broke order-service rate limits

symptoms.message: A configuration change that set the per-user order rate limit to 0 instead of 100 caused every order request to be rejected immediately with a 429 Too Many Requests response. The change was applied via a config map update and took effect without a service restart.

error_signature: 2026-07-18T09:00:04Z WARN order-service [rate-limit] request rejected: rate_limit=0 user_id=usr-8841 (config_map=order-limits version=v47)
root_cause: Config map update set the per-user rate limit to 0 due to a typo in the Helm values file, causing all order requests to be rate-limited immediately

fix_steps.step: Revert the config map to the previous version with rate_limit=100
fix_steps.note: Order requests resumed within 30 seconds of the config map revert taking effect

resolution: Reverted the config map to restore the rate limit to 100, immediately clearing the 429 responses.
runbook_summary: Identify the config change that caused the regression, revert to the previous config version, verify error rate recovers, and add config validation to the CI pipeline.
impact: 88% of order requests were rejected for 20 minutes.
lessons: Config changes must be validated against a schema that rejects zero or negative rate limits
Apply config changes with a canary phase before full rollout

title: Cache stampede on search-service trending results

symptoms.message: The trending-results cache key expired simultaneously across all search-service pods during a high-traffic afternoon peak. More than 5,000 concurrent requests hit the database at the same moment, spiking database CPU to 91% and causing search latency to exceed 8 seconds. Request coalescing was not enabled on the trending key.

error_signature: 2026-07-28T12:30:03Z WARN search-service [cache] stampede detected: key=trending:global concurrent_misses=5213 db_cpu_pct=91
root_cause: Cache stampede on the trending-results key due to synchronised TTL expiry across all pods and missing request coalescing

fix_steps.step: Enable request coalescing on the trending-results key to prevent parallel database reads
fix_steps.note: Concurrent database reads collapsed to 1 per expiry event and CPU dropped to 34%

fix_steps.step: Warm the cache by pre-loading the trending-results key every 5 minutes with a background job
fix_steps.note: Ensured the key was always warm, preventing future stampedes on this key

resolution: Enabled request coalescing and set up a cache-warming background job, eliminating the stampede and restoring normal search latency within 32 minutes.
runbook_summary: Enable single-flight coalescing on hot keys, pre-warm high-traffic keys with a background job, add TTL jitter, and monitor concurrent-miss rates.
impact: 24% of search users experienced high latency and partial errors for 32 minutes.
lessons: All cache keys serving high-traffic queries must have request coalescing enabled
Background warm jobs prevent stampede for known high-traffic keys

title: Missing database index causing full table scans on inventory-service

symptoms.message: After a schema migration that added a new warehouse_id column to the inventory table, queries filtering on warehouse_id started performing full table scans instead of using an index. With 12 million rows in the inventory table, each scan took 3 to 8 seconds, causing p95 latency to jump from 120 ms to 6,500 ms.

error_signature: 2026-08-06T09:59:51Z WARN inventory-service [db] slow query detected: 7243ms SELECT * FROM inventory WHERE warehouse_id=? (rows_examined=12048311 rows_returned=842 plan=full_table_scan)
root_cause: The schema migration that added the warehouse_id column did not include a corresponding index, causing full table scans on all warehouse-filtered queries

fix_steps.step: Add a database index on the warehouse_id column using a concurrent index build to avoid table lock
fix_steps.note: Index built in 12 minutes; p95 latency dropped from 6,500 ms to 110 ms immediately after

resolution: Added a concurrent database index on warehouse_id, reducing query time from 7 seconds to under 110 ms.
runbook_summary: Identify slow query from explain plan, build index concurrently to avoid lock, verify latency improvement, and add index coverage check to the migration CI step.
impact: 16% of inventory queries were severely slow for 45 minutes.
lessons: Schema migrations must include index creation for any filterable column
Add slow-query alerting at 2-second threshold

title: Database connection pool exhaustion on checkout-api during flash sale

symptoms.message: During a flash sale event the checkout-api database connection pool exhausted at 20 connections as concurrent checkout requests surged 5x above normal. The same pool-exhausted error pattern as INC-104 appeared in logs. Checkout orders failed with 503 responses for 30 minutes until the pool was expanded.

error_signature: 2026-08-22T12:00:07Z ERROR checkout-api [db] connection pool exhausted: waited 30000ms for connection (pool_size=20 checked_out=20 overflow=0) flash_sale=true
root_cause: Database connection pool size was not scaled up before the flash sale event, exhausting under 5x normal concurrency

fix_steps.step: Increase the database connection pool size to 100
fix_steps.note: Pool expanded and checkout orders immediately began succeeding

fix_steps.step: Restart the checkout-api pods to release any held connections
fix_steps.note: Pool utilisation settled at 22% after restart with the expanded pool

resolution: Increased the database connection pool size to 100 and restarted checkout-api pods, restoring checkout operations within 30 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify pool exhaustion from logs, increase pool size, restart service to clear held connections, and pre-scale pool before future high-traffic events.
impact: 50% of checkout users received 503 errors for 30 minutes during the flash sale.
lessons: Pre-scale connection pools before planned high-traffic events
Add pool-utilisation alerting at 70% to allow proactive action

title: Bad deployment on payment-service broke 3DS flow

symptoms.message: Release v4.5.0 of payment-service broke the 3DS authentication flow due to an incorrect redirect URL format introduced in the new payment gateway abstraction layer. Customers attempting 3DS-required payments received a blank redirect page and their transactions were declined. Only 3DS transactions were affected; non-3DS payments continued normally.

error_signature: 2026-09-10T08:45:11Z ERROR payment-service [3ds] invalid redirect_url format: got 'null/3ds/callback' expected 'https://pay.example.com/3ds/callback' release=v4.5.0
root_cause: Release v4.5.0 introduced a null base URL in the 3DS redirect URL builder when the PAYMENT_BASE_URL environment variable was not set in the new gateway abstraction layer

fix_steps.step: Scale out the payment-service to add more pods
fix_steps.note: Scaling out replicated the broken release and did not fix the redirect URL bug

fix_steps.step: Roll back to release v4.4.2 to restore the working 3DS flow
fix_steps.note: 3DS redirect URLs were correct immediately after rollback and transaction success rate recovered

fix_steps.step: Verify that the PAYMENT_BASE_URL environment variable is set and correct in all pods
fix_steps.note: Confirmed root cause and documented for v4.5.0 re-release checklist

resolution: Rolled back to release v4.4.2 and verified environment variable configuration, restoring the 3DS flow within 60 minutes.
runbook_summary: Identify broken release, roll back to last known-good version, verify fix, check all required environment variables before re-deploying the new release.
impact: 21% of payment transactions requiring 3DS authentication failed for 60 minutes; approximately 3% of affected customers did not retry successfully.
lessons: All required environment variables must be validated at startup; fail fast if missing
3DS flows must be included in pre-deploy smoke tests
